- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 70+ prices) by forecasting further upward; cap or dampen forecast after 2–3 consecutive high values.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast values are above 70, reduce by 1–2 points unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true trend by 1–2 days; if true outcome shows sharp rise after forecast, adjust next period’s forecast upward by 0.5–1.5 points.
- If sentiment history shows volatility (alternating 0.3–0.7), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecasts with weighted average of 3–5 prior values.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is near 68–70, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.0 point buffer to avoid missing upward momentum.
